title: Capacity of the general two-way channel
formal: Determine \(F_{\mathrm{TW}}(\mathrm{W},\lambda )=\sup _{(R_{1},R_{2})\in C_{\mathrm{TW}}(\mathrm{W})}[\lambda R_{1}+(1- \lambda )R_{2}]\) for every finite-alphabet discrete memoryless two-way channel W and real \(\lambda \in [0,1]\), allowing both terminals to adapt their inputs to past received outputs as defined below.
context:
Each of two terminals sends its own message while receiving information from the other. Its past observations can influence later transmissions, so the benefit of interaction is part of the capacity question. Removing that causal dependence would produce a different model.

The weighted capacity function records the rate tradeoff between the two directions. The target permits a mathematical description of this function with the stated certified error. Existing bounds and multiletter descriptions provide source context, but an unevaluated operational definition is not the requested determination.
why: Determines the fundamental value of interaction in simultaneous bidirectional communication.

definitions: W is a table of arbitrary real conditional probabilities \(\mathrm{W}(y_{1},y_{2}|x_{1},x_{2})\) on nonempty finite alphabets \(X_{1},X_{2},Y_{1},Y_{2}\), with nonnegative entries summing to one over outputs for each input pair. Node i holds \(M_{i}\), uniform on \(\{1,\ldots ,K_{i},n\}\), and the messages are independent. At time t in a block of n joint uses, node i sends \(X_{i},t=f_{i},t(M_{i},Y_{i},1,\ldots ,Y_{i},t- 1)\) for a deterministic function \(f_{i},t\). Given these inputs and the entire prior history, the output pair is drawn according to W. Node 1 estimates \(M_{2}\) from \((M_{1},Y_{1}^{n})\), and node 2 estimates \(M_{1}\) from \((M_{2},Y_{2}^{n})\), using deterministic decoders. Error is the probability that either estimate is wrong, averaged over messages and channel draws. A nonnegative pair \((R_{1},R_{2})\) is achievable when codes on \(n_{j}\to \infty\) uses have error tending to zero and \(\liminf _{j} (\log _{2}K_{i},n_{j})/n_{j}\ge R_{i}\). Thus \(R_{1}\) is the rate from node 1 to node 2, and \(R_{2}\) is the reverse rate. \(C_{\mathrm{TW}}(\mathrm{W})\) is the closure of achievable pairs. The channel law and all coding functions are public. There are no extra communication links, shared messages, input constraints or computational bounds; the received symbols themselves are the allowed feedback. Time sharing is predetermined. The capacity region is compact, convex and downward closed, and the full nonnegative supporting function determines it. \(F_{\mathrm{TW}}\) is in bits per simultaneous joint channel use, with no additional factor of two for the two directions. W is a mathematical real probability table, not an oracle with unspecified precision.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real-valued function g on every channel W defined below and every real \(\lambda \in [0,1]\), and prove in Lean that |\(g- F_{\mathrm{TW}}(\mathrm{W},\lambda )|\le 1/100\) pointwise throughout that domain, in the units stated in the definitions. The answer must establish lower and upper bounds with this uniform error guarantee. An exact determination also qualifies. A finite set of sample values, an uncertified plot, or a restatement of the defining optimization or limit does not determine the curve. No predetermined formula grammar or polynomial evaluation-time requirement is imposed. This numerical acceptance criterion does not assert exact equality with a conjectured curve.

sentences: Two terminals communicate independent messages in opposite directions through one memoryless channel.
Each transmitted symbol may depend on the sender’s message and its previously received symbols.
The target is the weighted capacity function of the resulting interactive rate region.
Rates count bits per simultaneous joint use, and the Lean tolerance is absolute error 0.01 for every channel and weight.
A result that forbids adaptation would address a different channel-coding problem.
